_doc: E2 worked-example fixture — FROZEN, READ-ONLY. Pins the E2 tie-break expected origin for the assessment.py / fault_report rewrite (MASTER-SPEC v7 §3, §6.3, §11, build F3). Authored by hand BEFORE the build run; hash-pinned by the §10 prerequisite gate. A build phase MUST NOT regenerate or edit this file (a self-authored expected result is a tautology). Loader contract: IGNORE every key whose name begins with '_' (annotations); consume only `registry`, `records`, `outcomes`; hold `expected` OUT-OF-BAND (do NOT let the implementation read `expected` — feed it only registry+records+outcomes and compare its output to `expected`).
_purpose: Two SCORED outcomes with DISTINCT origins, plus a distractor decision, so that ONLY an ev_id-matched causal selector + a corroboration-count-aware attribution rule satisfies BOTH. Every cheaper selector (latest/earliest/lowest-seq/fewest-inputs/t-match/time-window recency) and every cheaper attribution rule (always-attacker-key/length==1/count-claimer-own-key/read-runtime-classification) fails at least one scored outcome. See _discrimination for the enumerated kills.

_consume.causal_selector: for each outcome, select its causal decision by walking driving_input_seqs -> message -> signed_payload.payload.ev_claim.ev_id == outcome.ev_id (NOT by recency, junction, seq, input-count, or timestamp).
_consume.attribution_rule: over the causal decision's driving_input_seqs, recompute the INDEPENDENT-corroboration count (a signed input is INDEPENDENT iff its key != the claimer's key AND it is a sighting/claim from a distinct entity); count==0 -> attacker-key (attributed to the claimer key); count>=1 with >=2 keys -> corroborated. Signing-key-count is 1+ here (validly-signed messages), so the count==0 case resolves to attacker-key, NOT keyless-lone-sighting/sensor-fed-spoof (which needs key-count==0).
_consume.origin_is_class_independent: origin is decided ONLY from verified provenance (key-count + recomputed corroboration + ev_id link); it does NOT read the runtime `classification` field, nor the claimer's authorized entity-class. J-ATT's registry class is intentionally unspecified — it does not affect origin.
_consume.clocks: signed_payload.t = logical message tick (100-104); decision.t = sim time (150); outcome.t = harm-detection sim time (160, AFTER all decisions) — so a time-window/recency selector includes all decisions and picks the DISTRACTOR (latest), which is wrong for both outcomes.
_consume.scored_origins: only the 3 provenance-decidable classes are scored (§2/§3): keyless-lone-sighting->sensor-fed-spoof, uncorroborated-signed->attacker-key, corroborated. This fixture asserts attacker-key (o1) AND corroborated (o2).

records._note: attacker phantom advance-claim #2 (SAME key att-fpr, SAME ev_id EV-PH) — makes D_phantom a >1-input decision so a 'length==1->attacker-key' or 'fewest-inputs' shortcut diverges from the right answer

D_PHANTOM (harmful, causal for o1): 2 driving inputs, BOTH the claimer's own key att-fpr -> independent-corroboration count == 0 -> attacker-key. runtime classification LEGITIMATE (naive-victim admitted it) is NOT read for origin.
honest B INDEPENDENTLY corroborates EV-REAL (key hB != claimer hA)

D_LEGIT (causal for o2): 2 driving inputs, hA claim + hB independent sighting -> independent-corroboration count == 1 (>=2 keys) -> corroborated. SAME runtime classification LEGITIMATE as D_phantom but DIFFERENT origin, so a rule keyed on runtime classification cannot produce both.

D_DISTRACTOR (referenced by NO outcome): the LATEST-seq decision at J1 and the FEWEST-inputs (1) decision -> a latest/highest-seq/fewest-inputs selector picks THIS for both outcomes, which is wrong for both. Forces the ev_id walk.

outcomes._note: harm = the phantom preemption; detection t=160 is AFTER all decisions (t=150) so a time-window recency selector includes all and picks the distractor (seq 10)
review of the genuinely-corroborated preemption; SAME junction + SAME detection t as o1, DISTINCT ev_id -> only an ev_id-keyed selector distinguishes o1 from o2

expected.rationale: o1.ev_id 'EV-PH' matches the ev_claim in messages seq 3 & 4, which drive decision seq 5; seq 5's driving_input_seqs = [[3,att-fpr],[4,att-fpr]] are BOTH the claimer's own key, so recomputed independent-corroboration count == 0. The driving inputs are validly-SIGNED messages (signing-key-count == 1, NOT keyless), so the count==0 branch resolves to attacker-key, NOT sensor-fed-spoof (which requires key-count==0). Attributed to key att-fpr. runtime classification LEGITIMATE is IGNORED for origin (§3). system-classifier is NOT triggered: its predicate needs a logged-failed corroboration check contradicted by an independently-signed sighting in the window, which is absent (the AI wrongly ADMITTED, it did not wrongly reject).

o2.ev_id 'EV-REAL' matches the ev_claim in message seq 6, which (with sighting seq 7) drives decision seq 8; seq 8's driving_input_seqs = [[6,hA-fpr],[7,hB-fpr]] carry >=2 keys with hB's sighting INDEPENDENT of claimer hA -> independent-corroboration count == 1 -> corroborated (legitimate, no single culprit key). This is the NON-attacker scored case; an 'always attacker-key' rule fails here.

kills: latest-at-junction / highest-seq -> seq 10 (distractor): wrong for o1 AND o2
earliest-at-junction / lowest-seq -> seq 5: correct for o1 but WRONG for o2
time-window recency (window ends at outcome.t=160, includes all t=150 decisions) -> latest = seq 10: wrong for both
t-match (outcome.t=160) -> no decision has t=160: picks nothing / forces another rule
fewest-driving-inputs -> seq 10 (1 input): wrong for both
length==1 -> attacker-key -> seq 5 has 2 inputs so gives corroborated: WRONG for o1
count the claimer's own key as corroboration -> seq 5 count 0->2: flips o1 to corroborated: WRONG
read runtime classification for origin -> both causal decisions are LEGITIMATE but origins differ (attacker-key vs corroborated): cannot produce both
